history.summary: Identity confirmed: a well-documented hilltop Shakta shrine at Punkal Gaon, Galajwari, near Jaitunwala/Panjabiwala, about 15 km from Dehradun city, at ~2,083 m altitude on the right bank of the Nun Nadi. Legend: Princess Santala, daughter of a Nepalese king, fled to Dehradun with her brother Santaur Singh to escape a Mughal king (ETV Bharat names Aurangzeb) who wanted to marry her. Cornered by Mughal forces, the siblings prayed and were turned into stone idols in a flash of divine light that blinded the soldiers; the shrine was later built at the spot (built 'within the fort', per trawell). Saturdays are regarded as the most auspicious day. Reached by a ~2 km trek (about 700 steps) up through pine forest from Panjabiwala village. FLAG: coordinates are approximate - pinned to Punkal Gaon village centre (verify); the hilltop shrine sits on the ridge above. Opening hours conflict across sources (verify).

name: Santala Devi Temple
town: Panjabiwala/Punkal Gaon (CSV town 'Dehradun' is the city, ~15 km away)
town_description: Dehradun is the capital city of Uttarakhand, set in the Doon Valley at the foothills of the Himalayas. Panjabiwala (Punjabiwala) and Punkal Gaon are villages north of the city past Garhi Cantt and Jaitunwala, from where the Santala Devi hill rises to 2,083 m with views over the Doon Valley and Garhwal hills.

travel.road: Drive via Garhi Cantt to Jaitunwala, then to Panjabiwala village (12 km from Dehradun); the temple is a ~2 km trek (about 700 steps) uphill from the village

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (best for the trek); avoid monsoon (July-September) when the path is slippery
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 6:00 AM-7:00 PM (trawell, uttarakhanddiaries, earthtrip) vs 8:00 AM-6:00 PM (dehraduntourism, promallu) vs 7:00 AM-12:00 PM and 2:00-6:00 PM (uktravelcompany) - verify before visiting
